definition: Nvidia Drive is a computer platform by Nvidia, aimed at providing autonomous car and driver assistance functionality powered by deep learning.
details: The platform was introduced at the Consumer Electronics Show (CES) in Las Vegas in January 2015. An enhanced version, the Drive PX 2 was introduced at CES a year later, in January 2016. The closely platform related software release program at some point in time was branded NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion along with a revision number helping to match with the generation of hardware it is created for - and also creating ready to order bundles under those term. In former times there were only the terms Nvidia Drive SDK for the developer package and sub-included Nvidia Drive OS for the system software (aka OS) that came with the evaluation platforms or could be downloaded for OS switching and updating later on.

explainer.lead: Nvidia Drive is a computer platform from Nvidia aimed at autonomous cars and driver assistance powered by deep learning. It matters as an end-to-end hardware and software base for vehicle AI.

tiers.eli5: It is the computer inside a car that watches the road with cameras and sensors and helps the car drive.
tiers.practitioner: Automotive engineers build driver-assistance and autonomous features on the platform; the pitfall is matching the software release to the exact hardware generation, which is why releases carry a revision number tied to that generation.
tiers.paperLevel: Drive is a computing platform for autonomous and driver-assistance functions powered by deep learning; its related software program has been branded NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion with a revision number matching the hardware generation.

explainer.example: Drive PX 2, an enhanced version of the platform, was introduced at CES in January 2016.
